thesis: This is a mono-green deck that spends the three turns which are not yours: Radagast opens one discounted flash window per player turn, a creature walks through each one, a card-per-body engine pays for the creature, and the accumulated board is cashed in by a mass-pump finisher — whose verified threshold is the FIFTH body, not the finisher.

stages.label: MANA YOU DO NOT SPEND
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-six deliberately plain lands plus a two-humped ramp class (18 cards, RAMP drawn by t6 at 93.6%) — but the job is not casting bigger things sooner. The job is having something left over when it is somebody else's turn. A tapped-out Radagast deck has three dead windows a round, so this stage is measured by what stays UNSPENT. Castle Garenbrig is the emblem: its six {G} burst is spend-restricted to creature spells, which makes a liability elsewhere the best land here, and it is load-bearing in three passing stacks. Sakura-Tribe Elder, Elvish Reclaimer and Wood Elves sit on both sides of the ramp/body line; Wood Elves is filed under fuel because it is the canonical window body.
cards: Bala Ged Recovery // Bala Ged Sanctuary

evidence.note: Garenbrig's six restricted {G} cannot pay for Chord of Calling (an instant) but its plain {T}: Add {G} can — the restriction is the deck's shape written onto a land
Garenbrig pays for Craterhoof; it is in three of seven passing stacks
GREEN ON CURVE holds only the lands with text; 30 Forests and the whole ramp class live in MANA ON LEGS (city-1) and THE SEARCH PARTY (city-5)

stages.label: FOUR WINDOWS A ROUND
stages.what_it_does: Radagast has to resolve. His one ability grants the turn's FIRST creature spell both a {2} discount and as-though-flash, and 'each turn' means every player's turn — four windows per round in a four-player pod, verified. Nothing else in the deck happens on schedule until he is down: the metronome bodies, the flash traps and the card-per-body engine are all downstream of the window existing. Yeva, Nature's Herald is the only backup and she covers half the ability: flash for every green creature spell, deck-wide, but no discount and no once-per-turn reset. Answering Radagast therefore does not answer the deck — it answers the price.

evidence.note: the discount and the flash both applied on an opponent's turn; the window recurs per turn, not per round, and only for the FIRST creature spell
a body flashed on the end step before yours satisfies both prongs of 302.6 — end-step flash is functionally haste, so the window costs no tempo
the window is a creature-spell permission only; an instant neither uses it nor consumes it
coincidental agreement worth naming: THE WIDE BOARD holds both because they are green creatures among green creatures, not because the map can see the window

stages.label: ONE BODY PER WINDOW
stages.what_it_does: The window consumes one creature per turn, and the declared METRONOME class (19 cards, 3–5 MV with at least 2 generic — the band the {2} discount pays off fully) is what it eats: a body drawn by t6 in 94.5% of runs, mean turn 1.615. These are the members whose job is only to be a body at the right price. Mirkwood Pathmaker is the odd one and the important one: its power equals your land count, which makes it the deck's greatest-power dial — see the undeclared coupling in map_disagreements.

evidence.note: Wood Elves cast for {G} on an opponent's turn — the class's canonical member, and the most load-bearing non-commander card at five passing stacks
Hornet Nest and Scute Swarm on the board are what a finisher pumps; Scute Swarm appears in three passing stacks
9 of the declared 19 sit in THE WIDE BOARD; the rest scatter over four more cities

stages.label: A CARD PER BODY
stages.what_it_does: The engine proper: it turns bodies into cards, which become bodies. Ten cards, GAS drawn by t6 at 75.9%. There is no `fodder` stage in this deck — nothing sacrifices, nothing is consumed. What the engine actually converts is a resource other decks throw away: mana that is still untapped when the turn passes. Glademuse is the purest statement of that ('whenever a player casts a spell, if it's not their turn, that player draws') and it is symmetric. Selvala is the deck's only declared single point of failure — a one-card class at 12.3% by t6 — though stack 007 shows Chord finds her at instant speed.

evidence.note: Beast Whisperer's cast trigger fires on the finisher itself — the kill spell also draws a card
Fecundity converts a wrath into four cards; the token triggers before it ceases to exist and Radagast's death is seen before he moves to the command zone
Frostfang plus Toski draw exactly 2 off one unblocked 1/1 — the trap and the gas are the same card
Chord of Calling at X=3 puts Selvala onto the battlefield at instant speed, but triggers no Beast Whisperer: she is put, not cast
7 of 10 sit in A CARD PER BODY; Selvala files under mana, Toski under armour, Harmonize under the wide board

stages.label: ANSWERS THAT COME DOWN AT INSTANT SPEED
stages.what_it_does: What the window produces besides bodies: interaction on somebody else's turn, mostly wearing a creature. Whiptongue Hydra has no printed flash and costs six — it exists as a post-blockers sweeper only because the window makes it one. Chord of Calling is the exception that proves the shape: verified in stack 007 to take no discount, consume no window, refuse Garenbrig's restricted mana and trigger no Whisperer — the tutor sits outside the engine entirely. Boseiju is filed under mana but the audit counts it as one of the seven artifact/enchantment answers, and Collector Ouphe answers by disabling rather than destroying, so the declaration does not count it at all.

evidence.note: the flagship trap: a creature flashed after blockers changes combat damage already lined up
the negative line — three separate ways Chord refuses Radagast's gifts

8 of 10 sit in THE TRAPS; only Chord (THE SEARCH PARTY) and Collector Ouphe (THE WIDE BOARD) stray. This is the deck's second most map-coherent stage, because 'destroy target artifact' is printed on the card

stages.label: THE INSURANCE ON ONE WIZARD
stages.what_it_does: The deck is linear on Radagast and on one board, so this stage is what stops a single removal spell or a single wrath from being the whole game. Guardian Augmenter flashes in and grants the commander hexproof; Saryth blankets untapped creatures with hexproof and gives tapped ones deathtouch; Sylvan Safekeeper, Heroic Intervention, Tyvar's Stand, Veil of Summer, Inspiring Call and Warg Tactics are held, not cast — which costs nothing here, because the deck was holding mana anyway. Toski belongs functionally in this stage too and is filed under conversion; its indestructibility is verified in stack 004 and its draw in 002.

evidence.note: the wrath case: Toski's indestructibility is what survives Day of Judgment, and Fecundity turns the wrath into four cards
exactly THE BODYGUARDS, minus Toski, which the map files here for its indestructibility and this model files under conversion for its draw

stages.label: THE FIFTH BODY
stages.what_it_does: A mass-pump alpha strike over a wide board. Four finishers, drawn by t6 at 42.4% and assembled with a second wave at 40.2%. Stack 003 measured the arithmetic honestly and it is the most important number in the deck: X=5 over four bodies is 36 unblocked into a 40-life seat — four short. The FIFTH pre-Craterhoof body is the trigger, not the Craterhoof. Stack 005 then found the one card the deck's signature verb is wrong for: flashed on the prior end step, Craterhoof's +6/+6 and trample expire at that turn's cleanup, so the kill is cast from your own precombat main and the flash mode is a wrath-dodge only. Only Craterhoof scales on creature COUNT and brings its own haste and trample; Overwhelming Stampede and Pathbreaker Ibex multiply by greatest power, and Return of the Wildspeaker is a flat +3/+3 with no trample whose other mode is a draw spell.

evidence.note: 36 unblocked over four bodies leaves the seat at 4; a fifth pre-Craterhoof body (X=6) clears 40
the pump ends at 514.2 cleanup — the end-step flash line attacks with 10 unpumped power and kills nobody
4 of 4 in THE WIDE BOARD, the only component that is fully coherent by function — because 'creatures you control get +X/+X' IS the function, printed on the card

lines.note: Cast on an opponent's turn for {G}: the discount and the flash both applied because Wood Elves was that turn's first creature spell. One window per turn, four per round.

A body flashed on an opponent's end step meets both prongs of 302.6 by your untap: it attacks and it taps freely. Deploying on other people's turns costs no tempo, which is what makes holding mana affordable.
The cast trigger fires on the finisher itself — the turn the deck tries to win, it also draws a card.

Under Day of Judgment you draw 4: the Insect token's zone-change trigger fires before it ceases to exist, indestructible Toski skips the wake, and Radagast's death is seen before he moves to the command zone. The wrath refills the hand.

Flashed after blockers, Frostfang's static deathtouch applies to damage already lined up; Toski's 1 kills a 6/6 and one unblocked 1/1 draws exactly 2. In this deck the trap and the gas are frequently the same card.
Garenbrig's six {G} is spend-restricted to creature spells, which is why a land that would be a liability in most decks is the best one here.
X=5 over four bodies is 36 into a 40-life seat — four short. The fifth body is the trigger.

The one card the window is wrong for. Flashed on the prior end step, the +6/+6 and trample end at that turn's cleanup (514.2) and the swing is 10 unpumped power. The kill is cast in your own precombat main; the flash mode buys only a wrath-dodge, at the cost of the pump.

The negative line, and the sharpest boundary of the engine: Chord is an instant, so it takes no discount, consumes no window, cannot be paid with Garenbrig's restricted six, and fires no Beast Whisperer — and the creature it finds is put onto the battlefield rather than cast, so no cast trigger fires at all.

map_disagreements.component: A METRONOME body drawn (3-5 MV, >=2 generic — the full-value flash-in class)
map_disagreements.why: The class is defined by a COST BRACKET crossed with a permission printed on a different card. No member of it says anything about being a metronome body — they say 'draw a card', 'destroy target artifact', 'create a token' — so the map files each one under what it says and the class has five addresses. The law the scatter table demonstrates: a component is coherent on this map exactly when its defining property is printed on its members. THE OVERRUN KILL is 4-for-4 in one city because 'creatures you control get +X/+X' is the function; the metronome is invisible because the function lives on the commander.

map_disagreements.component: A FLASH TRAP drawn (instant-speed interaction wearing a creature body, or held protection)
map_disagreements.why: The map splits cards that ARE instants (THE BODYGUARDS: Heroic Intervention, Veil of Summer, Tyvar's Stand) from cards the window MAKES into instants (THE TRAPS). The deck runs them as one class and pays for them with the same held mana. Whiptongue Hydra is the case in point: six mana, no printed flash, and the deck's premise card.

map_disagreements.component: GAS drawn — a repeatable draw engine
map_disagreements.why: Seven of ten sit in A CARD PER BODY, so this one is nearly coherent. The three strays each show the map choosing one of a card's two jobs: Selvala files under mana because she taps for it, Harmonize files under the wide board as a plain draw sorcery, and Toski files under armour because its printed text is about being indestructible and unblockable. Toski is the sharp one — the map reads a bodyguard, the deck runs a draw engine, and both readings are verified: stack 002 for the draw, stack 004 for the armour.

map_disagreements.component: RAMP drawn (either hump: a dork/rock-class accelerant or a land-ramp spell)
map_disagreements.why: NOT a disagreement, and worth separating from the others. The declaration itself says 'either hump', and the map found exactly those two humps: dorks in MANA ON LEGS, land ramp in THE SEARCH PARTY. A component that spans cities BY DESIGN is a different finding from one that spans them because its function is unwritten.

Five cards multiply by the single largest power on your board — Overwhelming Stampede and Pathbreaker Ibex for their pump, Return of the Wildspeaker for its draw mode, Selvala for both her draw gate and the size of her mana ability — and one card in the 99 exists to set that number: Mirkwood Pathmaker, whose power equals your land count. This coupling appears in no declared component and in no city, because 'greatest power among creatures you control' is a NUMBER, and a number is not a subject that text clustering can see. It is the largest thing in this deck that neither the map nor the goldfish declaration knows about.

open_questions.question: Whiptongue Hydra flashed in after blockers are declared: does its ETB sweep the fliers before combat damage, how many +1/+1 counters does it keep, and does it kill your own Hornet Nest tokens and Hornet Queen tokens in the process?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the deck's premise card — a six-mana creature with no printed flash that is only an answer because the window makes it one — and the FLASH TRAP class's only verified member is Ohran Frostfang, whose stack proves a point about deathtouch, not about a creature functioning as removal. The premise is unverified, and the collateral question is live: three of this deck's own token makers produce fliers.

open_questions.question: Can Scute Swarm alone reach the fifth body? With six or more lands its landfall creates a copy of itself per land entering; how many bodies does the board hold on the turn before Craterhoof, counting one land drop plus a fetch from Wood Elves or Sakura-Tribe Elder?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 003 established that four bodies plus Craterhoof is four damage short and the fifth body clears 40. Scute Swarm is the only card in the 99 that manufactures bodies without spending a window, so it is the deck's cheapest route to the one threshold a verified stack has already priced.

open_questions.question: Does Mirkwood Pathmaker function as this deck's greatest-power dial? With N lands, what is the X on Overwhelming Stampede and Pathbreaker Ibex, how many cards does Return of the Wildspeaker draw, and does Selvala's 'power greater than each other creature' gate then shut off for every subsequent body?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Two of the four finishers, the finisher-that-is-really-a-draw-spell, and the deck's single declared point of failure all multiply by one number that one card sets — and no component declares it, no city holds it, and no passing stack touches it. It is also the one place where the coupling may run backwards: a large Pathmaker could suppress Selvala's draw trigger for the rest of the game.

open_questions.question: Glademuse reads 'whenever a player casts a spell, if it's not their turn, THAT PLAYER draws a card.' Against a pod with instant-speed decks, does this deck net ahead on it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The strategic frame calls Glademuse 'tuned to this deck exactly'. The oracle text is symmetric and pays whoever casts, so the claim is really that this deck casts off-turn more than the table does. That is a real claim about the format, not about the card, and nothing in the artifacts checks it.

open_questions.question: With Yeva on the battlefield and Radagast answered, is the SECOND green creature spell of a turn castable at instant speed — i.e. does the deck retain the timing half of its identity at retail prices, and can a turn hold two bodies when both are out?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Yeva is the ignition stage's only redundancy and this model asserts she covers the timing half but not the discount and not the once-per-turn reset. That assertion is currently a reading of two oracle texts with no stack behind it, and it is the load-bearing claim about what happens after the removal spell everyone at the table is holding for the commander.

open_questions.question: How much of the metronome's real output is the simulator missing? The declaration's own note says the sim models neither Radagast's discount, nor aura ramp (Utopia Sprawl, Wild Growth, Fertile Ground), nor opponent-turn flash casts.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every rate quoted in this model — 94.5%, 93.6%, 75.9%, 42.4%, 40.2% — is a floor for a deck whose entire design is the three things not being modelled, and the size of the gap is unknown. Three columnists will quote these figures; they should know which direction they are wrong in.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: THE OVERRUN ASSEMBLED: finisher AND a second wave to pump (a metronome body as proxy for board width)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Replace the one-metronome-body proxy with the threshold stack 003 actually measured: the finisher plus four other bodies. At minimum, record in the note that the proxy is three bodies looser than the verified kill condition.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Stack 003 resolved the arithmetic: Craterhoof at X=5 over four bodies is 36 unblocked into a 40-life seat, four short, and a fifth pre-Craterhoof body clears it. The declaration prices 'assembled' at finisher-plus-one and measures 40.2% by t6, so the only kill rate this deck has is measured against a condition a passing stack says is not sufficient. This is the single most consequential figure in the deck and it currently answers an easier question than the one it is asked.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: GAS drawn — a repeatable draw engine (all but Harmonize gate on power 4+ entering; the declared thin engine)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Correct the parenthetical. Only Garruk's Uprising gates on power 4+; Elemental Bond and Tribute to the World Tree gate on power 3+; Selvala gates on greatest power among creatures. Beast Whisperer (any creature spell cast), Fecundity (any creature dies), Toski (combat damage to a player) and Glademuse (any off-turn cast) carry no power gate at all.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Six of the ten members do not care how big the creature is, and the deck's window bodies are frequently 1/1s (Wood Elves, Llanowar Elves, Sakura-Tribe Elder). A reader sizing the engine against this deck's actual board from the label would conclude the gas does not run. The membership is right; the sentence describing it is not.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: An answer to an artifact or enchantment drawn (the breadth floor; Boseiju is a land the sim counts as drawn)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add Ravenous Sailback. The component names seven; the deck holds eight.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Ravenous Sailback's ETB is 'choose one — this creature gains haste; or destroy target artifact or enchantment', which is exactly the function the component measures. The omission understates the breadth floor by a card, and the omitted card is a creature — which in this deck also means it arrives at instant speed through the window, unlike Beast Within or Pick Your Poison.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: SELVALA — the single best engine card, drawn (a declared one-card class: no functional backup exists in the 99)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Amend the note to record the tutor route: Chord of Calling at X=3 puts Selvala onto the battlefield at instant speed, verified in stack 007.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: This is the deck's only single point of failure, priced at 12.3% by t6, and the label states flatly that no backup exists. A passing stack demonstrates a route to her that the label denies. The hypergeometric on a one-card class is still correct — the claim about the deck is not.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: THE OVERRUN KILL: a mass-pump finisher drawn (Craterhoof class — needs a board, which the bodies rates price separately)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Either split Return of the Wildspeaker out of the Craterhoof class or note what it is not: +3/+3 flat, no trample, non-Human creatures only (the deck runs three Humans), and a modal card whose other half is a draw spell.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: The class is priced as four interchangeable finishers at 42.4% by t6. Craterhoof scales on creature COUNT and brings haste and trample; Stampede and Ibex multiply by greatest power; Return does neither and grants no evasion. Over the 1/1-heavy board this deck actually assembles, they are not the same card, and the redundancy claim is the reason the wincon stage lists Craterhoof as a single point of failure despite a nominal four-of.

findings.claim: the mechanical gate passes
findings.note: `.venv/bin/manamap pilot validate-engine radagast` → OK: 7 stages, 71 cards placed, 0 unassigned, 9/9 lines verified by a passing stack. Completeness re-checked by hand: 26+2+10+11+10+8+4 = 71 = the number of distinct entries in cards.json, so nothing is silently missing. deck-audit freshness block: goldfish_metrics.json and mana_analysis.json both carry decklist_sha256 231d89ab… and are current, so no quoted rate is stale.

findings.claim: 94.5% METRONOME, 93.6% RAMP, 75.9% GAS, 42.4% KILL, 40.2% ASSEMBLED, 12.3% SELVALA, mean turn 1.615; Wood Elves in five stacks, Garenbrig in three, Scute Swarm in three
findings.note: Every one re-derived. `engine-facts radagast --json` audit_engine by_turn_6_rate: 0.945 / 0.936 / 0.759 / 0.424 / 0.402 / 0.123, METRONOME mean_turn 1.615 — exact matches, and each is correctly labelled 'by t6' rather than the assembled_rate the audit prints (0.981 / 0.975 / 0.854 / 0.523 / 0.513 / 0.163). verified.by_card: Wood Elves 001/003/004/005/007 (5), Castle Garenbrig 003/005/007 (3), Scute Swarm 003/004/005 (3). City counts also hold: fuel 9-of-19 in THE WIDE BOARD, conversion 7-of-10 in A CARD PER BODY, output 8-of-10 in THE TRAPS with only Chord and Collector Ouphe straying, wincon 4-of-4, protection == city-3 minus Toski exactly.

findings.claim: one discounted flash window per player turn; a card-per-body engine pays for the body; the verified kill threshold is the FIFTH body, not the finisher
findings.note: Stack 001 final_state confirms the window resets per turn ('four windows per round in this four-player pod — but only the FIRST creature spell each turn'). Stack 003 final_state: X=5 over four bodies = 36 into 40, opponent survives at 4, 'a fifth pre-Craterhoof body (X=6, six attackers) would clear it'. Stack 005 final_state independently lands on exactly 40 trample power off a five-body board in the main-phase line. The thesis does not out-run either stack, and it names the deck's real resource (mana left over on other people's turns) rather than a better story.

findings.claim: GREEN ON CURVE holds only the lands with text; 30 Forests and the whole ramp class live in MANA ON LEGS (city-1) and THE SEARCH PARTY (city-5)
findings.note: Two errors in one sentence, both against the map block of engine-facts. (1) city-4 GREEN ON CURVE's card list literally contains 'Forest', and its own gloss reads 'Thirty-six lands with almost nothing to say' — the Forests are exactly where the model says they are not. (2) The RAMP scatter is MANA ON LEGS 8 / THE SEARCH PARTY 5 / THE WIDE BOARD 4 / GREEN ON CURVE 1, i.e. four cities; Utopia Sprawl, Wild Growth, Fertile Ground and Rampant Growth sit in THE WIDE BOARD. The model states this correctly in map_disagreements[3] and incorrectly here, so it disagrees with itself as well as with the artifact.

findings.claim: Yeva 'covers half the ability: flash for every green creature spell, deck-wide, but no discount and no once-per-turn reset', and whether a second green creature spell is castable at instant speed is a load-bearing open question for resolve-stack
findings.note: cards.json: 'You may cast green creature spells as though they had flash' — no per-turn limit at all, and the deck is mono-green, so Yeva is strictly BETTER than Radagast on timing (every creature spell, every turn) and worse only on cost. 'no once-per-turn reset' reads as a limitation on Yeva when the absence of the limit is the point. Consequently open_questions[4]'s first half is settled by the oracle text and does not need a stack spawn; only the two-bodies-in-one-turn interaction is genuinely open. The Radagast SPOF claim itself survives: a grep of the 99 for 'less to cast' returns exactly one card.

findings.claim: the declared METRONOME class is '19 cards, 3–5 MV with at least 2 generic — the band the {2} discount pays off fully'
findings.note: Four of the nineteen fall outside the stated band, checked card by card against cards.json: Satyr Wayfinder ({1}{G}, MV 2, one generic), Eternal Witness ({1}{G}{G}, MV 3, one generic), Whiptongue Hydra (MV 6) and Hornet Queen (MV 7). The size (19) and the rate are right; the description is not, and the model added the gloss 'the band the {2} discount pays off fully' as its own claim rather than quoting. This is the same defect class the model correctly catches in proposed_goldfish_edits[1] for the GAS parenthetical — a sixth proposed edit is owed for this label.

findings.claim: 'Ten cards, GAS drawn by t6 at 75.9%'
findings.note: The conversion stage's `cards` array holds eleven: the ten declared GAS members plus Fauna Shaman, which is in the TUTOR component, not GAS. The rate belongs to the 10-card declaration and the sentence reads as describing the stage. Contrast stages[2], which says 'the declared METRONOME class (19 cards)' explicitly and is unambiguous. Three columnists read this file; 'ten cards' beside an eleven-card list is the kind of figure that gets quoted.

findings.claim: There is no `fodder` stage in this deck — nothing sacrifices, nothing is consumed
findings.note: The conclusion is right; the supporting sentence is false as written. Grepping the 99 for 'sacrifice': Sakura-Tribe Elder ('Sacrifice this creature: search your library for a basic land'), Caustic Caterpillar ('{1}{G}, Sacrifice this creature'), Sylvan Safekeeper ('Sacrifice a land'), Elvish Reclaimer ('{2}, {T}, Sacrifice a land') and Tireless Provisioner's Food/Treasure tokens. Sakura-Tribe Elder's sacrifice is the mechanism behind this model's own lines[1]. 'No sacrifice THEME, so no fodder stage' is defensible; 'nothing sacrifices' is not.

findings.claim: the protection stage, evidenced by stack 004 and city-3
findings.note: Stack 004's scenario names Fecundity, Radagast, Scute Swarm, Toski and Wood Elves — none of the stage's eight cards. So every member of this stage is evidenced by a city (a location) plus oracle text, and no interaction involving Guardian Augmenter, Saryth, Sylvan Safekeeper, Heroic Intervention, Tyvar's Stand, Veil of Summer, Inspiring Call or Warg Tactics is verified anywhere in this deck. The oracle claims I checked are accurate (Guardian Augmenter: Flash + 'Commanders you control have hexproof'; Saryth: other untapped creatures hexproof, other tapped creatures deathtouch — the 'other' qualifier is dropped, which matters for Saryth herself). The honest form is either a city-only evidence block that says so, or an open_question for resolve-stack; the stack citation as written implies verification the stage does not have.

findings.claim: Craterhoof Behemoth is the wincon stage's single point of failure despite a nominal four finishers
findings.note: Nothing tests the alternatives — no stack in the deck resolves Overwhelming Stampede, Pathbreaker Ibex or Return of the Wildspeaker — and the model's own map_disagreements[4] undercuts it: Mirkwood Pathmaker's power equals your land count (cards.json: P/T are '*'), so on the eight-land board where an 8-MV Craterhoof is castable, Overwhelming Stampede (MV 5, no discount available since it is a sorcery) pumps by ~8 and also grants trample, against Craterhoof's X = creature count (6 in stack 005). Stampede needs no haste either — it pumps creatures already on board, whereas Craterhoof needs its own. The audit prices the class at four cards and the model gives no evidence that three of them are non-functional. State it as 'Craterhoof is the largest and the only one that scales on count' (true) or open a stack; 'single point of failure' is a stronger word than the file earns.

findings.claim: from: fuel → to: conversion, via Beast Whisperer + Craterhoof Behemoth, verified_by 003
findings.note: The mechanism is verified — stack 003 step 1 has the Whisperer trigger resolving off the Craterhoof cast — but neither via card is in the `fuel` stage: this model files Beast Whisperer under conversion and Craterhoof under wincon. The arrow's stated endpoints are connected by no card in the line. `validate-engine` cannot see this (it only checks that the stack's scenario names the via cards), and the renderer draws the arrow between the two boxes. Correct endpoints are wincon → conversion.

findings.claim: from: fuel → to: output, via Ohran Frostfang + Toski + Llanowar Elves, verified_by 002
findings.note: The note is exactly right — stack 002's summary confirms deathtouch applying to already-declared attackers via 604.2/704.5h and 'you draw exactly 2 cards' — but no via card is in either endpoint stage: Frostfang and Toski are both in conversion, Llanowar Elves is in mana. Neither `fuel` nor `output` contains any of the three. The verified content is a conversion-side claim (combat damage becomes cards) that the arrow files as fuel→output.

findings.claim: from: output → to: ignition, via Chord of Calling + Radagast + Garenbrig + Beast Whisperer, verified_by 007
findings.note: Stack 007's final_state verifies three NEGATIVES: Chord neither uses nor consumes Radagast's window, cannot be paid with Garenbrig's restricted mana, and fires no Beast Whisperer (Selvala is put, not cast). The stack therefore refutes any flow between these stages, while `lines[]` is the structure that says the engine flows from one stage to the next and is drawn as such. As a boundary statement this is the most valuable paragraph in the file; as a line entry it is a passing stack cited beneath an arrow it disproves. It belongs in the ignition stage's evidence (where the same stack is already cited correctly) or in a prose field, not in lines[].

findings.claim: 'Five cards multiply by the single largest power on your board'
findings.note: Four are then named: Overwhelming Stampede, Pathbreaker Ibex, Return of the Wildspeaker, Selvala. A grep of all 71 entries in cards.json for 'greatest power' returns exactly those four, so the enumeration is complete and the count is wrong (Selvala contributes two abilities, not two cards; Mirkwood Pathmaker is excluded by the sentence's own construction as the setter). One imprecision inside it: Return of the Wildspeaker reads 'greatest power among NON-HUMAN creatures you control' and the deck runs three Humans — the model knows this (proposed_goldfish_edits[4] says so) and drops the qualifier here. Selvala's draw gate is also 'greater than EACH OTHER creature's power', i.e. it compares against opponents' creatures too, which makes the suppression worry in open_questions[2] stronger than stated, not weaker.

findings.claim: the greatest-power coupling 'appears in no declared component and in no city ... the largest thing in this deck that neither the map nor the goldfish declaration knows about'
findings.note: The axis is REAL — I verified every text, including Mirkwood Pathmaker's 'power and toughness are each equal to the number of lands you control' — and the 'no declared component' half is right (no goldfish target groups them). But the map does hold it: engine-facts map.cities city-0 THE WIDE BOARD contains Overwhelming Stampede, Pathbreaker Ibex, Return of the Wildspeaker AND Mirkwood Pathmaker; only Selvala (city-1 MANA ON LEGS) strays. That is 4 of 5 in one city — by this model's own coherence law (map_disagreements[0]: coherent exactly when the defining property is printed on the members) it is close to coherent, since 'greatest power among creatures you control' IS printed on three of them. Rewrite as 'no declared component knows about it, and the map has it four-fifths right'.

findings.claim: replace the one-body proxy with 'the finisher plus four other bodies — the threshold stack 003 actually measured', the proxy being 'three bodies looser than the verified kill condition'
findings.note: Finisher-plus-four-bodies is precisely the configuration stack 003 measured as NOT lethal: 36 damage, opponent alive at 4. The verified threshold is the finisher plus FIVE bodies — stack 003 ('a fifth pre-Craterhoof body (X=6, six attackers) would clear it') and stack 005 (five bodies + Craterhoof in the main phase = exactly 40 trample power, lethal to one seat). So the change prescribes the losing board, and the proxy is four bodies looser than the kill condition, not three. The diagnosis behind the edit is the most valuable thing in the file — the only kill rate this deck has (40.2%) is measured against a condition a passing stack says is insufficient — which is exactly why the number in it has to be right before a human applies it.

findings.claim: the GAS label's 'all but Harmonize gate on power 4+' is wrong; six of ten carry no power gate
findings.note: Checked every member against cards.json oracle text: Garruk's Uprising 'power 4 or greater' (the only 4+); Elemental Bond 'power 3 or greater'; Tribute to the World Tree 'draw a card if its power is 3 or greater'; Selvala 'if its power is greater than each other creature's power'; Beast Whisperer 'whenever you cast a creature spell'; Fecundity 'whenever a creature dies'; Toski 'combat damage to a player'; Glademuse 'whenever a player casts a spell, if it's not their turn'; Ohran Frostfang combat damage; Harmonize a flat draw three. The membership is right and the parenthetical is wrong exactly as claimed.

findings.claim: the artifact/enchantment breadth component names seven cards where the deck holds eight — add Ravenous Sailback
findings.note: Verified both halves. goldfish_targets.json's component lists exactly seven: Caustic Caterpillar, Nantuko Vigilante, Wickerbough Elder, Boseiju, Beast Within, Pick Your Poison, Indrik Stomphowler. Ravenous Sailback is in the 99 and reads 'When this creature enters, choose one — this creature gains haste; or destroy target artifact or enchantment', which is the measured function. I also checked for a ninth: grepping the 99 for 'artifact or enchantment' and 'destroy target artifact' returns only those eight, and Collector Ouphe ('Activated abilities of artifacts can't be activated') is correctly excluded as a disabler. Also correct that Sailback is a creature and therefore arrives through the window, unlike Beast Within or Pick Your Poison.

findings.claim: the SELVALA label's 'no functional backup exists in the 99' should record the Chord route, verified in stack 007
findings.note: Stack 007's final_state verifies it: Chord at X=3 puts Selvala onto the battlefield at instant speed (X must be at least 3 because her mana value is 3), and she can tap for mana on your following turn. The label does deny what a passing stack demonstrates, and the edit correctly leaves the 12.3% hypergeometric alone. Incomplete rather than wrong on one point: Fauna Shaman is a second route (discard a creature card, search your library for a creature card) and is the other member of the declared TUTOR component; the amended note should name both.

findings.claim: Return of the Wildspeaker is not interchangeable with Craterhoof: +3/+3 flat, no trample, non-Human only (three Humans in the deck), modal with a draw half
findings.note: cards.json: 'Choose one — Draw cards equal to the greatest power among non-Human creatures you control; or Non-Human creatures you control get +3/+3 until end of turn' — flat, no trample, non-Human on BOTH modes. Type lines confirm exactly three Humans: Eternal Witness, Saryth and Sylvan Safekeeper. One point that strengthens the edit and is missing from it: Radagast's discount is creature-spell-only, so Overwhelming Stampede (sorcery, MV 5) and Return (instant, MV 5) can never use the window, while Craterhoof and Pathbreaker Ibex can — a second reason the four are not one class. Note this finding is `supported` while the related SPOF claim in stages[6] is not: 'not interchangeable' is earned, 'single point of failure' is not.
